Record source SHA, dirty-source hash if any, lock hash, output hash, WXT mode, loaded extension runtime ID, Chrome version, profile label, principal/role/org state, permission state, fixture IDs, and timestamp without secrets. Before opening Tools, satisfy the current resource permit and build/reload contract in docs/stabilization/PLAN.md. In the isolated profile, verify the loaded artifact and side panel match the receipt; reload the extension when required, reopen the side panel, and reload the controlled fixture tab. Run warm and post-reload/cold-recovery passes separately and preserve separate run evidence. No HMR-only acceptance.

Sign in as the role for that profile. Tools manual Run is the user-initiated direct local handler route: select All handlers (or Internal delegates if the row is grouped there), search the exact tool name, expand it, enter the stated JSON, press Run, and inspect the inline result. The route supplies permissionMode='act' and assignedTabId=null and bypasses dispatch.ts authorization/confirmation checks. These observations do not establish account authorization, registered agent invocation, or Ask/Act enforcement.

Preflight that the exact loaded Chrome artifact has the required downloads permission and chrome.downloads API. download_url and cancel_download declare required downloads permission in source/catalog; the combined downloads tool declares none in its wrapper schema but delegates into those handlers. Do not remove or toggle permissions to manufacture denial. Missing permission/API is a prerequisite gap or observed unavailable-API result, not proof of dispatcher denial.

Use a newly created dedicated disposable Chrome profile for each role, not a reused profile. Before adding fixtures or running any downloads action, confirm its Downloads history is empty. If it contains any row, stop and create another fresh profile; do not inspect or record those rows. Do not create the shared completed fixture for every case: create it only for EXT-F-4154 list/confirm, and create only the gated owned endpoint fixtures when they are actually available.

Never inspect, cancel, overwrite, delete, or report downloads from an existing/user profile. In each verified-empty disposable profile, stop if any unexpected row appears and do not copy its URL, path, or other details into evidence. For each owned download created, record its exact returned ID, filename, and final file path privately. After sanitized evidence capture, close Chrome, remove only those exact owned file paths and verify each is absent, retire the dedicated disposable profile and verify its exact profile directory is absent. If any ownership/path/absence is uncertain, do not delete it and mark cleanup unverified.
source_findings: ToolsView manual Run parses JSON, validates the local Zod schema, invokes handler.run directly, sets permissionMode='act', and sets assignedTabId=null; its source comment says this route skips the permission gate because it is user-initiated.
download_url calls chrome.downloads.download and then searches by the returned ID; it catches thrown errors and returns {ok:false, reason}. It has no assigned-tab dependency.
cancel_download calls chrome.downloads.cancel with the integer ID and returns {ok:true}; it does not catch API errors. It has no assigned-tab dependency.

downloads action=list delegates to list_downloads; action=confirm searches the supplied ID; action=cancel parses the string ID then delegates; action=download_url delegates with URL and optional filename. The canonical tool is tierFor(action): list is read and other actions are action.

The direct tool registry catalogs download_url and cancel_download with downloads permission. The inventory's 2026-10-04 exact-name live-binding census says those leaf names are absent while downloads is active; this historical snapshot does not prove current advertisement or runtime reachability.

EXT-F-4087-T01.title: Controlled manual execution: download_url
preconditions: Complete the shared receipt-bound setup independently for member and admin, including verified downloads permission/API in each exact loaded artifact/profile. Do not prepare the completed-download HTML fixture for this case.

Before attempting a positive call, provide a controlled owned HTTP(S) fixture endpoint with deterministic small synthetic bytes and a known expected filename. Such a source fixture is missing in this lane; until it exists and is reviewed, record this positive branch as fixture-pending and do not use a public or personal URL.
Use Tools > Catalog > All handlers (or Internal delegates when surfaced there), find download_url, and confirm its visible schema matches the checked-in handler before running.
steps: If and only if the owned controlled URL fixture is present, enter valid_args with its exact run-scoped URL and a unique synthetic filename; press Run. Record the returned download_id, returned filename, state, and ok value. If the fixture is absent, stop this branch as fixture-pending without invoking the handler.

In Chrome Downloads, verify only the returned ID/run-scoped filename: it belongs to this invocation, has the expected synthetic bytes and completed state, and its reported filename is consistent with Chrome's chosen name. Never assert against unrelated rows.
Run invalid_args. Expect the runner's schema validation error before handler invocation; verify no new owned download ID/file appeared.

Reload the extension and reopen the side panel under the required receipt-bound sequence. Repeat the valid fixture call with a new run-scoped filename only if the controlled fixture still exists; compare result and downloaded bytes, then record cold/recovery evidence separately.

After sanitized evidence capture, remove only exact owned file paths created by this case (including a partial file from the owned slow fixture), verify each is absent, close Chrome, retire this dedicated profile and verify its exact directory is absent. Do not remove any unidentified path; if ownership or absence cannot be confirmed, mark cleanup unverified.
expected: With a valid controlled URL and granted API, source predicts ok:true with download_id and filename; the returned state may be absent because the immediate search can race download state, so verify final state in Chrome Downloads by exact ID. Exact successful behavior remains runtime-unverified.
Malformed URL fails Zod validation in the manual runner and should not call chrome.downloads.download or create a file.

If the exact artifact lacks chrome.downloads, source handler returns {ok:false, reason:'downloads API unavailable'}; if Chrome rejects a URL or download operation, handler returns {ok:false, reason}. Record observed text sanitized; do not claim this tests dispatcher denial.
If the owned endpoint fixture is missing, there is no positive result; keep the case unverified/fixture-pending.
uncertainty: No owned HTTP(S) source for a direct download_url call exists in the reviewed fixture set; successful URL/filename behavior and Chrome's immediate search state are not observed.
Manual Catalog Run bypasses dispatcher checks; Ask/Act, role authorization, current live binding, and agent-advertised execution remain unverified outside this case.

steps: In the verified-empty profile, first run {"action":"list"} and confirm the full returned downloads array is empty.
